scope: Positive damping gives a unique finite-basis response vector at every real frequency, including resonance. The residual norm divided by the damping bounds the error in the vector.
The doubled system in Eq. (12) is Hermitian. A vector supported on the second block solves it exactly when its nonzero component solves the original response equation.
Reciprocal eigenvalue weighting solves the damped response equation in the supplied energy eigenbasis.
Summing the two frequency branches gives the excited-state sum for dipole polarizability in Eq. (3). The permanent ground-state dipole cancels.
